This study investigated the presence of tick-borne bacteria in ticks collected at a​ veterinary clinic in northern Veracruz, Mexico. A total of 164 Ornithodoros puertoricensis ticks were identified using morphological characteristics and 16 S mitochondrial ribosomal RNA sequencing. DNA extracts were screened by conventional PCR for Borrelia, Rickettsia, Bartonella, Coxiella, and Ehrlichia/Anaplasma, followed by DNA sequencing and phylogenetic analyses of positive samples. Borrelia puertoricensis DNA was detected in six ticks (3.66%), in four nymphs and two females. Phylogenetic analyses of the flaB gene confirmed that all sequences clustered within the B. puertoricensis clade with strong bootstrap support. In addition, a Coxiella endosymbiont was detected and assigned to clade B based on 16 S rRNA phylogenetic reconstruction, representing the first molecular evidence of this lineage in O. puertoricensis. None of the DNA samples were positive for Rickettsia, Bartonella, Ehrlichia, or Anaplasma. These findings provide the first molecular evidence of B. puertoricensis and a Coxiella clade B endosymbiont in O. puertoricensis from Veracruz, extending the known distribution of both microorganisms in Mexico. The detection of these bacteria in ticks collected at a veterinary clinic capable of treating wild animals highlights the importance of integrated acarological and molecular surveillance at wildlife-domestic animal-human interfaces to improve understanding of the ecology and public health significance of neglected tick-borne zoonoses.

papers.title: Type II GM1 Gangliosidosis with Intrafamilial Variability: A Case Series of Five Affected Siblings.
papers.abstract: GM1 gangliosidosis is a rare, autosomal recessive, progressive, neurosomatic lysosomal storage disorder caused by GLB1 gene variants. The disease demonstrates significant phenotypic heterogeneity, with poor genotype-phenotype correlation. We describe a familial case series of five affected siblings presenting with a variable spectrum of disease manifestations. Clinical evaluation was performed in all siblings, whereas biochemical investigations and neuroimaging were performed in the proband and next-generation testing was performed in two severely affected sibling. Variant interpretation was carried out using standard American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG) criteria and phenotype based re-annotation tool. Genetic testing identified compound heterozygous GLB1 variants - c.1325G > A and c.326G > C, confirming the diagnosis of GM1 gangliosidosis. Although the age of onset was similar (6-7 years) in most siblings, variability was observed in disease severity, neurological manifestations and progression. This series highlights the importance of molecular diagnosis in children presenting with unexplained neuroregression. Early genetic confirmation facilitates appropriate genetic counselling, supportive care and prenatal diagnosis.

papers.title: Development and clinical validation of a multiplex PCR-based targeted next-generation sequencing panel for simultaneous DNA/RNA pathogen detection in respiratory tract infections: a comprehensive performance evaluation.
papers.abstract: Lower respiratory tract infections (LRTI) remain a leading cause of global morbidity and mortality, with approximately 62 % of cases lacking definitive etiological diagnoses via conventional methods. This study aimed to develop and validate a multiplex PCR-based targeted next-generation sequencing (mp-tNGS) panel for comprehensive pathogen detection in respiratory samples. We conducted a combined retrospective (n=209) and prospective (n=256) study involving 465 bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) samples from patients with suspected LRTI. The mp-tNGS panel was designed to detect 277 clinically relevant pathogens, integrating simultaneous DNA/RNA co-detection and single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP)-based contamination control. Diagnostic performance was evaluated against conventional microbiological tests (CMTs) and metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS). The mp-tNGS assay revealed a limit of detection (LoD) of 25 copies/mL for bacteria/fungi and 50 copies/mL for viruses, with acceptable precision (intrabatch CV=9.42 %; interbatch CV=26.03 %). A novel SNP-based bioinformatics pipeline achieved exceptional discriminative performance (AUC=0.992) for distinguishing true infections from contamination. Compared with CMTs and mNGS, mp-tNGS showed superior sensitivity (93.59 %, 95 % CI: 90.81-95.73 %), particularly for viruses (AUC=0.92 vs. 0.845). The assay reliably identified fastidious pathogens (e.g., Pneumocystis jirovecii and Legionella pneumophila ) and predicted antimicrobial resistance (97.08 % concordance with phenotypic testing). We developed an mp-tNGS panel with diagnostic performance comparable to that of mNGS. The panel integrates broad pathogen coverage, rapid turnaround time, machine learning-based false-positive reduction, and concordance with phenotypic susceptibility testing, positioning it as a promising molecular diagnostic tool for LRTI.

papers.title: Nationwide molecular survey of Babesia and Theileria DNA in wild rodents and mites collected from rodents in Korea.
papers.abstract: Piroplasm parasites of the genera Babesia and Theileria are widely distributed in wildlife and are maintained through complex host-vector transmission systems. Rodents play important roles as reservoir hosts for various arthropod-borne pathogens; however, comparative investigations integrating multiple host compartments and host-associated ectoparasites remain limited. In this study, we conducted a nationwide molecular survey of Babesia and Theileria species in wild rodents and mites collected from rodents in Korea. Rodent blood and liver tissues, together with mite pools, were examined using PCR-based detection methods, and spatial and seasonal variation in pathogen detection patterns was evaluated. Babesia microti was detected in both rodent blood and liver tissues, with higher positivity in blood and marked spatial and seasonal heterogeneity. The higher positivity observed in blood was consistent with the intraerythrocytic biology of B. microti, although differences in analytical sensitivity between sample types were not evaluated. Theileria capreoli DNA was detected exclusively at low frequency in mite pools, whereas Theileria luwenshuni DNA was detected at low frequency in both rodents and mite pools. Because mites are not established biological vectors of these Theileria species, detections in mite pools were interpreted as molecular occurrence rather than evidence of transmission or vector competence. Significant regional and seasonal variation was observed in blood and mite samples; however, overall detection frequencies were low, warranting cautious ecological interpretation. This nationwide, multi-compartment assessment highlights the ecological complexity of piroplasm circulation in wildlife systems and underscores the importance of integrated surveillance approaches when interpreting parasite DNA detection in arthropod assemblages.

papers.title: Draft genome sequence of basidiomycete yeast Rhodotorula mucilaginosa DH4148 from a patient with fungemia.
papers.abstract: Rhodotorula mucilaginosa is a basidiomycete yeast with ecological and emerging clinical relevance. Here, we report a high-quality de novo genome assembly of R. mucilaginosa strain DH4148 isolated from a patient with fungemia.

papers.title: A Portable, Quick-Visualization Platform for Field Detection of Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense Tropical Race 4 ( Foc TR4) in Banana.
papers.abstract: Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense ( Foc ) is a soilborne fungal pathogen that causes Fusarium wilt of banana (FWB), leading to multiple outbreaks worldwide and resulting in severe economic losses. In the absence of any effective fungicides or soil disinfectants for this disease, rapid in-field detection of this pathogen is essential for early intervention and containment. However, current in-field detection methods still rely on instruments, making the process time-consuming and complex. Herein, we developed a portable and ultra-fast detection assay for Foc Tropical Race 4 (TR4), the most destructive Foc lineage, based on recombinase polymerase amplification (RPA) with lateral-flow dipstick (LFD) readout. We identified a TR4-specific DNA fragment as the diagnostic target and prepared crude templates using a room-temperature lysis buffer, eliminating the need for DNA purification. All RPA components, except the template primer-probe mix and magnesium acetate, were lyophilized in a single Eppendorf tube to simplify the workflow and avoid step-by-step reagent addition, allowing the reaction to be conducted in the field by hand or using a portable metal bath. The developed RPA-LFD system offers a high specificity toward Foc TR4, showing no cross-reactivity with other Foc strains, and achieved a limit of detection of 10 fg/μl in the field. This sensitivity enables the detection of infections in asymptomatic plants at early stages. This platform provides a convenient, ultra-fast, and user-friendly tool for on-site Foc TR4 surveillance and supports timely management decisions to curb the spread of FWB.

papers.title: DeePEn - A Depth sensitive benchmark for Protein Engineering
papers.abstract: Recent progress in modeling techniques and high-throughput screening has significantly enhanced the accessibility of protein engineering. Nevertheless, further progress gets hindered by the lack of robust benchmarks that capture the practical challenges for real-world protein engineering. Here, we introduced DeePEn, a Depth-sensitive benchmark for Protein Engineering that quantifies model generalization to held-out variants at increasing mutational distance from the wild type. We defined distance as the number of simultaneous point mutations, i.e., single amino acid variants (SAVs), moving from wild-type to mutant (edit distance in computer science jargon). DeePEn retrospectively evaluates prediction and prioritization using experimentally labelled variants from deep mutational scanning (DMS) datasets; it does not benchmark prospective sequence generation or goal-directed optimization. Specifically selecting four DMS datasets with sufficient multi-mutation data points from ProteinGym, we assessed recent predictive models, including general and biophysics-informed protein Language Models (pLMs), and a non-transformer neural network. Our results highlight how the performance of all models deteriorates with increasing mutational distance and that no single metric sufficiently captures the diverse requirements of protein engineering. To overcome these shortcomings, DeePEn provides a readily available resource for multi-metric benchmarking that focuses on variant-effect prediction of variants distant from the wild type.

papers.title: Brain states recur during longitudinal viewing and relate to content across narratives and sensory formats
papers.abstract: Models of brain dynamics propose that brain activity revisits a repertoire of configurations, and that current input influences which configuration is expressed. How broadly this holds across a person's extended experience is unknown. We analyzed 38-57 hours of fMRI per participant in six adults watching the television series Friends. Participant-specific hidden Markov models identified 42-47 active brain states, and independent fits to separate portions of viewing recovered similar states with similar tendencies to recur. States matched across participants' separately fitted models tended to occur at the same moments of the episodes. Among states retained after temporal screening, features from pretrained video, audio, and language networks partly predicted state identity, most strongly from intermediate-to-late layers. Predictions learned from Friends generalized without retraining to new films, and language-based predictions extended to reading and audiobook listening. State usage corresponded across stimuli little beyond what each recording's spectra and covariance reproduced.

papers.title: Coarse-tuning to improve a protein foundation model for a domain of proteins: the example of outer membrane beta barrels
papers.abstract: Foundation models for proteins have shown great potential in addressing a wide range of challenges in computational molecular biology. State-of-the-art models are trained on large and diverse corpora of protein sequences, enabled by self-supervised training. The models are then used in transfer learning and the embeddings they calculate are used in supervised downstream tasks. We propose a novel focusing mechanism for foundation models, which we call 'coarse-tuning'. In coarse-tuning, we further update the model, using a defined yet unlabeled, dataset to enhance its performance in a specific domain. We demonstrate this approach using Outer Membrane Beta Barrels (OMBBs) - proteins that are found in the distinct biophysical environment of the outer membrane. Our results show that coarse-tuned models outperform the original foundation model when applied to various transfer learning tasks. Additionally, we study the embeddings generated by the coarse-tuned models and compare them to those from the original foundation model, including an investigation of the learned attention matrices via contact map predictions. Our work suggests that a medium-sized dataset (fewer than 100,000 protein sequences) is sufficient to effectively specialize a foundation model to a specific domain, enhancing its utility for domain-specific applications.

papers.title: Genetics and genomics of enteroarthroconidial development in Coccidioides
papers.abstract: Regulated cell death is a cornerstone of plant and animal development. Distant orthologs of some cell death genes are also found in microbes, with roles that remain incompletely understood. The human fungal pathogen Coccidioides causes the disease Valley fever when infectious spores called enteroarthroconidia are inhaled from soil. These spores develop via an unusual checkerboard-style differentiation in which alternating segments of hyphae (cellular filaments) die and disarticulate, releasing mature spores on either side. The molecular mechanisms are unknown. We first adapted single-cell transcriptomics for filamentous fungi, cataloguing expression across the specialized cells of a developing Coccidioides colony. With the resulting profiles, and cell-biological validation via protein tagging, we characterized high expression of the pyroptosis-like cell death pathway in hyphal segments destined to die. Next, we tested the function of pyroptosis-like pathway genes directly by genetic knockout; strains lacking these factors exhibited a phenotype of developmental arrest at a late stage in the colony, preserving hyphal growth but abrogating cell death and spore production. Together, these findings reveal the pyroptosis-like pathway as a requirement for enteroarthroconidial development, and thus infectivity, in Coccidioides. We propose that regulated cell death may prove to mediate events in development in many fungi with multicellular life cycles.

papers.title: A Proteome-Wide Gain-of-Function Atlas Mapping the Landscape of Chemotherapy Response
papers.abstract: Background: Conventional chemotherapies remain the core therapeutic backbone of cancer treatment, yet the rapid emergence of chemoresistance often compromises their clinical efficacy. Although large-scale functional genomics has transformed precision oncology, existing reference maps rely predominantly on loss-of-function paradigms and lack systematic data on gain-of-function (GOF) events that commonly drive clinical resistance. Methods: To address this gap, we engineered a site-specific Bxb1 integrase landing-pad system in HeLa cells, enabling single-copy integration of a human proteome-wide library [18,388 open reading frames (ORFs)] at the AAVS1 locus under a uniform EF1 promoter. We systematically profiled cellular fitness across 16 chemotherapeutics. We integrated this GOF perturbation screen with bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing, FACS-based lysosomal functional screening, clinical cohort survival analyses, and preclinical xenograft modeling. Results: Stratified modeling of over 230,000 gene-drug interactions defined distinct functional categories that are strongly enriched for clinical cancer biomarkers and prognostic relevance. Global network analysis and organelle-specific lysosomal functional screening uncovered that chemotherapeutic agents, most prominently the nucleoside analog TAS-102 (Lonsurf), converge upon a shared survival hub centered on the BCL-2 family-associated autophagy-endolysosomal network. Mechanistically, TAS-102 triggered lysosomal activation as an adaptive survival response. Co-treatment with the BCL-2 family inhibitor ABT-263 (Navitoclax) attenuated this TAS-102-induced lysosomal response and synergistically reversed TAS-102 resistance across colorectal and pancreatic cancer models in vitro and in colorectal cell line- and patient-derived xenograft (CDX, PDX) models in vivo. Conclusions: Our study establishes an open-access, proteome-wide GOF reference atlas that systematically maps chemotherapeutic responses, recapitulates canonical resistance biology, and nominates rational drug combinations. This systems-genomics resource bridges massive-scale perturbation mapping with actionable target discovery, providing a translational framework to overcome therapeutic resistance and reprogram cancer drug responses.

papers.title: Intellectual disability risk gene RFX4 regulates cortical neurogenesis by restraining neuronal differentiation
papers.abstract: Despite the recent identification of RFX4 as a neurodevelopmental disorder risk gene, its role in cortical development remained unclear. Here, we derived human stem cell models of deficiency and pathogenic mutation and demonstrated that RFX4 restrains neurogenesis by repressing pro-neuronal gene expression, while maintaining lineage-specific roles in regulating proliferation during cortical inhibitory neuron development. We also defined requirements for RFX4 in recruiting RFX3 to chromatin to regulate synaptic and activity-dependent gene expression in progenitors and neurons, respectively. RFX4 deficiency persistently dysregulated neuronal differentiation in cortical organoids, while not affecting neurons generated by direct differentiation. Finally, we modeled pathogenic mutation of the RFX4 DNA-binding domain, finding that DNA binding was strongly reduced but gene expression was dysregulated differently from our deficiency models, supporting a mechanism of pathogenicity distinct from haploinsufficiency. Together, this work identified requirements for RFX4 during cortical development, building a necessary foundation for elucidating the etiology of RFX4-associated disorders.

papers.title: Vermeer: Autoregressive generative modeling of microscopy predicts protein localization
papers.abstract: Fluorescent microscopy provides a rich view into how proteins localize within cells, but it remains experimentally infeasible to image human proteins across all of the different factors that can impact localization. We introduce Vermeer, a channel-adaptive autoregressive generative model for in silico generation of microscopy images of protein localization. Vermeer conditions generations on protein sequences and landmark stains showing the morphology of cells, which enables it to generalize to unseen proteins and cell lines. We show that Vermeer, trained on the Human Protein Atlas, can generate images with substantially improved perceptual quality and biological fidelity over previous proposals. Additionally, Vermeer's autoregressive framework enables flexible generation using varying channel subsets and orderings, enabling zero-shot transfer to data collected under different imaging conditions and channel configurations than those used for training. These results position Vermeer to enable scalable modeling of protein localization and is a step towards generative foundation models that can operate over distinct microscopy datasets. Code is publicly accessible at https://github.com/microsoft/vermeer.git.

papers.title: Detection of zoonotic Cryptosporidium parvum in invasive beavers from southern Tierra del Fuego, Chile
papers.abstract: Since their introduction to Tierra del Fuego in 1946, invasive beavers have expanded their population and caused extensive environmental degradation across the subantarctic region. Beaver dams have profoundly impacted peatlands, mature sub-Antarctic forests, and watercourses. Here, we report a pathogen in invasive beavers in Patagonia and discuss their potential role as a reservoir of waterborne zoonotic pathogens. We detected Cryptosporidium through microscopy using the Ziehl-Neelsen staining technique in beaver collected from southern Tierra del Fuego. Out of the 105 beavers examined, three tested positive to optical microscopy, which were then identified molecularly as Cryptosporidium parvum by sequence analysis of the 18S ribosomal DNA (rDNA). Given the potential impacts of Cryptosporidium parvum upon native species, wildlife, and human health, this finding highlights the potential risks associated with the ongoing expansion of beavers into other areas of the sub-Antarctic region. A potential role of invasive beavers as reservoirs of zoonotic Cryptosporidium spp. in Patagonia emphasizes the unknown consequences of human-introduced exotic species on pristine ecosystems.

papers.title: The Multi-scale Copula Index (MCI): a new information-theoretic measure of association and its applications in functional cancer genomics
papers.abstract: Cancer genomic analyses increasingly involve large, complex datasets representing diverse omics variables, such as gene expression, mutations, copy number alterations, genetic perturbations (e.g. CRISPR or iRNA), drug sensitivity, and clinical phenotypes, making it crucial to accurately measure associations among these variables. Traditional correlation-based methods, like the Pearson correlation coefficient, often assume linearity, Gaussian distributions, and independence among variables, leading to oversimplified assumptions, less sensitive readouts and less accurate significance estimation. Information-theoretic measures overcome these limitations by being one step removed from the data and assessing dependencies at the level of probability distributions, thus providing a more data-agnostic, robust measure for identifying associations in common analysis tasks such as feature selection, pattern recognition, and predictive modeling. Building on these foundations, we introduce the Multi-scale Copula Index (MCI), a novel information-theoretic measure of association. The MCI offers significant advantages over existing methods by eliminating the need for density estimation and parameter tuning, thereby ensuring consistent estimation with reduced computational complexity. Furthermore, it enhances statistical power at lower sample sizes, exhibits strong robustness to outliers, and successfully captures both directionality and important symmetries under input-data transformations, such as reflection or complementation. Due to these strengths, the MCI is particularly useful for functional cancer genomic applications involving, e.g., transcriptional and perturbational data, with different statistical properties across a wide range of dataset sizes and complexity. Contextual associations often arise in functional genomics datasets: two genomic variables show little or no correlation in most samples, yet display a strong linkage within the subset that reflects the active biological context. These situations are ideal for quantifying associations with the MCI. We illustrate the performance of the MCI in a variety of benchmarks and cancer genomic examples and applications. We also introduce the Cumulative Entropy Diagram (CED), a graphical display that allows the visualization of the MCI between a reference vector, such as a phenotype, pathway activation or drug response, and a complete set of genomic features.

papers.title: Multimodal protein representations across human brain cell types
papers.abstract: The central nervous system (CNS) comprises diverse cell types whose molecular context shapes the roles of the proteins they express. Computational models offer a scalable way to study the roles of proteins across human brain cell types, with protein language models and interactome- or single-cell-based models capturing complementary information encoded in protein sequences and cellular network contexts. Human brain tissue is hard to access, so brain cell types make up a small fraction of the atlases single-cell models train on and of the benchmarks used for their evaluation. To capture these complementary sources of information in the CNS, we introduce SEMPER, a multimodal representation learning model that aligns protein language model representations with protein-protein interaction networks from 442 cell types of the adult human brain, giving each protein a sequence-informed representation in every cell type in which its gene is expressed. We show that SEMPER representations predict cell type-specific protein complexes and predict genes essential to the survival of dopaminergic neurons, measured in a genome-wide CRISPR screen. In zero-shot retrieval, SEMPER recovers clinically pursued drug targets for Parkinson's disease, Alzheimer's disease, multiple sclerosis, Huntington's disease and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis at higher rates than cell type-specific models. To further improve target recovery, we combine SEMPER with a large language model that reasons over protein functional annotations. The combination recovers more targets, with SEMPER providing experimentally derived cellular context that complements literature-based reasoning of the large language model.

papers.title: A Three-Axis Framework for Therapy Prioritization in MBD4-Deficient Tumors: De-confounded Synthetic Lethality Modeling, Replication-Stress Pharmacology, and PARP1 Trapping Decoupling
papers.abstract: Background: Loss-of-function mutations in MBD4 (methyl-CpG-binding domain protein 4) cause a specialized base excision repair (BER) deficiency characterized by hypermutated CpG>TpG signatures and sensitivity to immune checkpoint blockade. However, post-immunotherapy treatment prioritization remains empirically unmapped. In clinical oncology, DNA damage response (DDR) defects are frequently extrapolated to poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitor (PARPi) sensitivity by analogy to homologous recombination deficiency (HRD), without testing whether upstream glycosylase loss generates the nicked single-strand break (SSB) intermediates required for toxic PARP1-DNA trapping. Methods: We developed a three-axis framework integrating mechanistic curation, large-scale pharmacogenomics (DepMap 24Q2 CRISPR/RNA-seq, n=1,517; GDSC2 dose-response profiling, n=928; PRISM Repurposing), and a 5-Layer De-confounded Synthetic Lethality Machine Learning (SL-ML) Engine (SL-XGBRanker). To prevent functional dilution from variants of uncertain significance, MBD4 loss-of-function (MBD4-LOF) was strictly restricted to truncating and canonical splice-site alleles (21 of 36 mutated lines), independently validated by nonsense-mediated mRNA decay (NMD; two-sided p2s = 0.0367), while excluding 15 lines harboring 19 non-truncating variants (18 missense, 1 inframe deletion). All primary pharmacogenomic comparisons were evaluated using two-sided Mann-Whitney U tests (p2s), bootstrap 95% confidence intervals (CIs), Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (BH-FDR) multiplicity correction across six pre-specified candidate axes, and Two One-Sided Tests (TOST) for expression equivalence. Results: Our analysis delineates three distinct therapeutic axes in MBD4-LOF tumors: (1) Cytidine Analog Vulnerability (Axis 1): Mechanistic structural evidence demonstrates that MBD4 loss impairs excision of 5-substituted pyrimidine analogs and deaminated bases, creating a direct biochemical bottleneck to gemcitabine and 5-fluorouracil incorporation. (2) ATR-Check1 Replication-Stress Vulnerability (Axis 2): In GDSC2 profiling, MBD4-LOF cell lines exhibit significant sensitivity to the ATR inhibitor ceralasertib (AZD6738). In the clinically relevant TP53-mutant background-which disables the G1/S checkpoint and forces reliance on ATR-mediated S/G2 arrest-MBD4-LOF lines (n=11 vs n=619 WT) demonstrate pronounced ceralasertib hypersensitivity (Delta LN_IC50 = -1.07, 95% CI [-1.62, -0.41], Cohen's d = -0.74, p2s = 0.0060, BH-FDR q = 0.036; Delta AUC = -0.087, d = -0.89, p2s = 0.0017), with 11/11 leave-one-out (LOO) jackknife iterations retaining two-sided significance (p2s <= 0.014). This genotype-associated dependency remains robust in the unstratified pan-cancer cohort (n=14 vs n=914 WT; Delta LN_IC50 = -0.73, 95% CI [-1.31, -0.11], d = -0.50, p2s = 0.0430; Delta AUC = -0.056, d = -0.56, p2s = 0.0259) and after purging microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H) lines (n=10 vs n=906 WT MSS; Delta LN_IC50 = -0.91, 95% CI [-1.50, -0.22], d = -0.62, p2s = 0.0307). By contrast, Wee1 inhibition (adavosertib; n=15 vs n=920 WT; Delta LN_IC50 = -0.35, p2s = 0.1667) does not reach statistical significance. (3) Absence of Single-Agent PARPi Sensitivity (Axis 3): While PARP1 transcript abundance strongly governs pan-cancer PARPi cytotoxicity across n=481 cell lines (rho = -0.416, p < 10^-21 across five clinical PARPi), MBD4-LOF tumors (n=19 vs n=1,498 WT) show zero compensatory PARP1 upregulation (median 6.77 vs 6.66 log2[TPM+1], Delta median = +0.11, 95% CI [-0.39, +0.71], p2s = 0.605; TOST equivalence p_TOST = 0.0199 within +/- 0.50 log2[TPM+1]). Direct GDSC2 evaluation of MBD4-LOF (n=8) versus WT (n=478) confirms complete absence of single-agent PARPi sensitization across talazoparib (p2s = 0.973), olaparib (p2s = 0.522), niraparib (p2s = 0.877), rucaparib (p2s = 0.804), veliparib (p2s = 0.538), and the composite 5-drug mean PARPi Z-score (Delta median Z = -0.024, 95% CI [-0.84, +0.60], p2s = 0.841). Under Leave-One-Anchor-Out cross-validation across 12 canonical DDR genes (370 gene-drug pairs), our 5-Layer De-confounded SL-ML Engine achieves an out-of-fold AUROC of 0.9716, AUPRC of 0.8007, and Top-1 accuracy of 82.86%, zero-shot ranking gemcitabine (#1) and ceralasertib (#2) as the top therapeutic dependencies for held-out MBD4 while rejecting all PARP inhibitors (ranks #13, #27, #28, #31). Conclusion: MBD4-LOF tumors exhibit a selective, TP53-potentiated pharmacological dependency on ATR kinase inhibition alongside mechanistic vulnerability to cytidine analogs, but lack both the nicked BER repair intermediates and the PARP1 target expression required for single-agent PARP inhibitor efficacy.

papers.title: CD19 CAR T cell therapy reshapes the host microbiota immune axis in autoimmune diseases
papers.abstract: CD19 targeted CAR T cell therapy induces profound B cell depletion and clinical responses in autoimmune disease; however, whether it reshapes host microbiota interactions remains unknown. We longitudinally profiled gut microbiome composition and microbiota-specific humoral immunity in 20 patients with systemic lupus erythematosus, systemic sclerosis, or idiopathic inflammatory myopathy undergoing CAR T cell therapy, alongside 23 healthy controls, using shotgun metagenomics, IgA/IgG-bound microbiota profiling, and PhIP Seq. CAR T cell therapy reshaped microbiota directed humoral immunity, with reduced fecal IgA and serum anti commensal IgA and IgG accompanied by selective remodeling of microbiota-reactive antibody repertoires. This finding was paralleled by selective changes in gut microbial composition, including depletion of Bifidobacterium adolescentis, without uniform depletion of disease-associated pathobionts. Integrated host microbiome analyses identified altered predicted protein protein interactions involving the immunoproteasome and B cell plasma cell pathways, with interactions before CAR T cell intervention being significantly associated with subsequent relapse. Consistent with these findings, taxon specific IgA targeting, but not global diversity of IgA IgG coated microbiota, differed according to subsequent relapse. Lower baseline fecal IgA was also associated with delayed B-cell reconstitution, linking mucosal humoral immunity to immune recovery after CAR T cell therapy.

papers.title: Blood-meal analysis indicates preferential feeding on humans and non-commensal rodents by Culex mosquitoes in Tanzania
papers.abstract: Arthropod-borne viruses are important emerging and re-emerging pathogens worldwide, yet information on mosquito feeding ecology and associated transmission networks remains limited in many African regions. This study investigated mosquito host-feeding patterns and arbovirus occurrence along an urban-rural gradient in Morogoro, Tanzania. Mosquitoes were collected at four locations representing different levels of human influence during wet and dry seasons. Vertebrate blood-meal sources were identified using a Nanopore-based metabarcoding approach, while viral screening was performed using RT-qPCR assays targeting Orthoflavivirus and Alphavirus genera. A total of 8,917 mosquitoes were collected, of which more than 90% belonged to the Culex genus. Blood-meal analyses of 310 blood-fed and gravid mosquitoes identified 35 molecular operational taxonomic units, which we grouped into 11 host categories. Humans were the most frequently utilized hosts (68%), followed by non-commensal rodents (22%) and crows (18%). Culex mosquitoes showed broad host use and frequently fed on multiple taxonomic units, with an average of 1.36 taxonomic units detected per individual. Co-feeding network analyses revealed extensive host sharing between humans and wildlife, with non-commensal rodents showing significantly higher co-feeding probabilities with humans than any other host group. No human-pathogenic arboviruses were detected. Viral detections were limited to insect-specific viruses, an endogenous viral element in chromosome 2 of Aedes aegypti, and two detections of bird-infecting Bagaza virus, indicating ongoing viral circulation within the mosquito community. Our findings demonstrate broad and flexible host use by Culex mosquitoes and highlight non-commensal rodents as an underappreciated component of mosquito feeding with potential relevance for arbovirus transmission and spillover between wildlife and humans.

papers.title: Climate change drives northward range shifts in invasive forest pests and pathogens
papers.abstract: Invasive tree pests and pathogens are increasingly threatening forests worldwide. Understanding how a warming climate and changing precipitation patterns will affect the future distribution ranges of these pathogenic species requires systematic analysis across a variety of host trees and pathogenic species. We analysed 31 major tree pests and pathogens that have caused widespread and extensive damage globally, predicting their current and future distribution under various climate change scenarios using species distribution modelling. Our results showed that tree pests and pathogens will consistently shift northward, threatening northern temperate and boreal forests between the years 2041 and 2080. On the other hand, some warmer regions, including southern Europe, were expected to experience fewer pest and pathogen outbreaks in the future. Annual mean temperature, mean temperature of the warmest quarter, precipitation of the warmest quarter, and precipitation of the driest month contributed to the species distribution models, indicating that warming temperatures and moderate precipitation may promote the survival, reproduction, and spread of the pathogenic agents. Our research highlights the need for enhanced monitoring, early pest and pathogen detection, stricter biosecurity measures, and improved silvicultural strategies in temperate and boreal forests in the northern hemisphere. Moreover, forest assessments, including those focused on carbon budgets, biodiversity, and ecosystem services, should account for the effects of tree pests and pathogen outbreaks, as they may drastically alter future functioning of forests globally.

papers.title: GeneEmbedLLM: Harnessing Large Language Models for Gene Functional Embedding and Association Prediction
papers.abstract: Effective and high-quality gene function representations are crucial for bioinformatics tasks. While biological knowledge about genes is inherently textual, encompassing functional descriptions and pathway annotations, current methods often rely on single-source, non-textual data, failing to capture the rich semantic information in multi-source gene annotations. In this paper, we propose GeneEmbedLLM, a Large Language Model (LLM)-powered framework for generating universal, semantically-aware gene embeddings. The proposed approach advances the gene representation learning through multi-source structured text integration from five authoritative databases and attribute-aware attention based on Longformer architecture and contrastive learning. Experimental results on diverse downstream tasks, ranging from molecular interactions and phenotypic dependencies to epigenetic regulation, confirm the validity and effectiveness of our proposed approach, where competitive performance is achieved across all evaluated benchmarks. We further validate the quality of the generated embeddings through comprehensive analyses, including embedding visualizations, intra-pathway similarity assessments, ablation study, and parameter analysis.

papers.title: ProLigGPT: a language model for protein-targeted ligand design free from structural constraints
papers.abstract: The deep-learning language model offers promising approaches to molecular design. However, existing models typically exhibit one or more of the following limitations: structural constraints, confinement to a single task, and lack of cross-domain capability (e.g., protein-to-ligand generation). Inspired by GPT's success in language modeling, we introduce ProLigGPT, a seq2seq autoregressive model based on GPT-2 and trained on ~1.9 million protein-ligand pairs without 3D structures. ProLigGPT supports tasks including de novo ligand generation and scaffold-based molecular design for target proteins. Benchmarking against three state-of-the-art structure-based models across eight representative target proteins, ProLigGPT demonstrated superior performance on comprehensive metrics. Through systematic evaluations of ProLigGPT's interpretability, we find that ProLigGPT uses the full protein sequence to generate target-aware ligands, unlike pocket-based strategies that depend only on residues near the binding site. Applying ProLigGPT to Pl3Kalpha; inhibitor design successfully yielded inhibitors with a novel scaffold and inhibitors derived from a known scaffold, demonstrating that ProLigGPT can reach beyond the boundaries of known chemical space. Finally, we validated the generalization ability of ProLigGPT on Target T1, which lacks a crystal structure and known inhibitors, confirming that ProLigGPT can design inhibitors solely from sequence information. These findings highlight the promise of language models in designing ligands for target proteins free from structural constraints, offering a flexible and scalable framework for exploring vast chemical spaces in drug discovery.

papers.title: Polysemanticity in human hippocampal neurons
papers.abstract: As we perceive language, neurons in the brain represent the meanings of each word we hear. Inspired by recent advances in the mechanistic interpretability of large language models (LLMs), we hypothesized that hippocampal neurons utilize polysemanticity, a coding strategy wherein individual neurons represent multiple semantically distant features. Polysemanticity increases capacity, robustness, and scalability, and facilitates contextualization. We find that during podcast listening, hippocampal single neurons exhibit dense semantic codes characterized by multiple tuning peaks. These peaks, corresponding to the stimuli that most effectively drive the neurons, are not random; instead, they have overdispersed, isotropic geometry, consistent with interference-minimizing repulsive coding, although they lack grid-like hexagonal structure. Individual neuron responses are strongly modulated by context while population geometry remains stable and generalizable, allowing for pattern separation without sacrificing generalizability. Together, these results indicate that hippocampal neurons represent meaning using a distributed, dense, contextualized, polysemantic code consistent with the demands of superposition.

papers.title: MicroDUET: a dual-headed genomic foundation model for pathogen surveillance
papers.abstract: Pathogen genomic surveillance works from raw reads, assembled genomes and alignments, representations that are slow and costly to compare at scale. Compact embeddings from genomic language models offer an alternative, but surveillance requires resolving both evolutionary ancestry (phylogeny) and phenotypic capability (function) - which need not co-vary. Here we present MicroDUET, which adapts a 26.6-million-parameter ProkBERT backbone with two 3.5-million-parameter adapter heads: a phylogeny head trained contrastively on genome windows from the same microbes, and a function head trained to identify genes across taxa. On held-out retrieval benchmarks, the phylogeny head returned the correct species for 80.3% and 66.6% of cellular and viral queries, and the function head the correct gene family for 97.3% and 97.2%, reaching 74.4% accuracy on an independent antimicrobial resistance-class benchmark. Across all three benchmarks MicroDUET outranked 17 other genomic encoders. Without training on lineage, clade or drug-susceptibility tasks, MicroDUET identified Mycobacterium tuberculosis and mpox virus lineages and clades (0.965, 0.975 accuracy), discriminated rifampicin resistance without lineage adjustment (AUROC 0.985), and retrospectively identified an emerging mpox lineage as anomalous (AUROC 0.974). MicroDUET operates 10^3 - 10^4 times faster than single-threaded sequence-based alignments. MicroDUET therefore provides a compact, reusable representation for scalable pathogen surveillance and sequence triage.

papers.title: Large language models complement established workflows for mechanistic model construction and refinement in systems biology
papers.abstract: Mechanistic models provide a framework for describing, understanding, and predicting biological processes, but their development requires an interdisciplinary team with expertise in biology, mathematics, and computation. Here we present Octomod, a multi-agent workflow based on large language models (LLMs) that integrates biological knowledge retrieval, model construction, parameter estimation, and hypothesis testing. Built on established software tools, including AMICI and pyPESTO, and community standards, including SBML and PEtab, Octomod supports model development and refinement through natural-language interaction with a user. The agents' proposals must pass defined checks and the user's decision before they are used. Every input, model, check, and decision is recorded, so that model building remains transparent and reproducible. We applied Octomod to four problems. Three used published data and differ in model size and in how much the user guided the run: Octomod constructed a model that matched a published model without user guidance, supported the interactive refinement of a gene-regulatory model, and built models of cell-cell communication that explained the responses of five immune cell types to different stimuli. In the fourth application, on newly generated and unpublished lipidomics data, Octomod helped to determine which processes the measurements could inform, identify unresolved label fluxes, and reduce a supplied model to those processes. Together, these results show how LLMs can strengthen and complement established workflows for constructing and refining biologically informed models.

papers.title: Benchmark Self-Triage (BeST): Comparing Self-Triage Systems and Multiple Generations of OpenAI Models Against Preliminary Expert Consensus
papers.abstract: As digital self-triage becomes more widely used, quality assurance requires evaluation of both emergency recognition and overall agreement with clinical judgement, including how these outcomes differ across generations of large language models. The Benchmark Self-Triage (BeST) project intends to provide a framework to compare systems for digital self-triage against a medical 'gold standard' in Germany. As a first step in developing and demonstrating the methodology, we compared study-specific implementations of SmED 5.4.11 accessed via API and Infermedica Engine API via Microsoft Azure Healthcare Agent Service with five structured OpenAI configurations spanning multiple model generations: gpt-4.1, gpt-5.4, gpt-5.6-luna, gpt-5.6-sol, and gpt-6-astra. The manufacturers of SmED and Infermedica offer MDR-certified Class IIb triage products, but these certified products were not directly evaluated. An LLM-based patient actor covered 480 physician-curated vignettes derived from German routine triage data. A pool of seven physicians provided preliminary reference classifications and consensus for 480 vignettes. Recommendations were mapped to three urgency categories-emergency, acute, and not urgent-and evaluated using winsorised weights derived from routine triage frequencies. Weighted emergency sensitivity ranged from 51.3% (95% CI 35.5-66.3%) for gpt-4.1 to 99.9% (99.7-100.0%) for gpt-6-astra. Weighted exact three-category agreement (accuracy) ranged from 54.4% to 68.8%; gpt-4.1 achieved the highest agreement despite the lowest emergency sensitivity. No system performed best across all urgency categories. The later-generation OpenAI configurations showed a more precautionary triage profile resembling SmED, with higher sensitivity for emergency cases; gpt-6-astra showed the strongest shift. This cross-sectional comparison across model generations suggests a shift towards more precautionary triage behaviour, without establishing a longitudinal improvement in accuracy. These findings highlight the limitations of overall agreement for evaluating self-triage and support category-specific assessment. Broader expert consensus and evaluation, as well as further steps to reduce dependence on SmED-derived source data, are needed and planned before drawing conclusions about clinical safety.

papers.title: Automating postmarketing pharmacovigilance with large language model agents
papers.abstract: Postmarketing pharmacovigilance relies on spontaneous adverse event reporting and labor-intensive observational studies, which suffer from underreporting and delayed risk detection. Large language model (LLM) agents could automate real-world evidence generation, but generalist agents make ad hoc analytical decisions that compromise epidemiological validity and reproducibility. Here we present MedCheckpoint, a multi-agent LLM system for automated postmarketing pharmacovigilance. MedCheckpoint grounds each analytical stage in a curated, source-traceable medical knowledge base, locks core study-design parameters before execution, performs patient-level analyses with human-written deterministic statistical tools, and enforces checkpoint rules that abort infeasible analyses, with optional human-in-the-loop review. We evaluated MedCheckpoint using a 54-question benchmark on a dual-purpose simulated electronic health record (EHR) testbed of 2.7 million individuals, designed with reliable clinical signals to evaluate routine analytical accuracy alongside spurious signals to stress-test system rigor. Across the benchmark, MedCheckpoint outperformed two coding-agent baselines in report quality across five dimensions rated by three independent LLM judges (overall means 4.81-4.88 versus 4.25-4.55 and 4.02-4.29) and yielded higher run-to-run consistency (mean within-question standard deviation 0.116-0.186 versus up to 0.440). Crucially, while baselines failed on up to 2 of 21 runs when handling infeasible comparisons or unmeasurable outcomes, MedCheckpoint produced no misleading failures across all seven stress-test trap questions with known data limitations. MedCheckpoint enables reliable, auditable, and scalable pharmacovigilance analysis.

papers.title: Nationwide Functional Profiling Enables Clinical Reclassification of KCNH2 Variants in the French LQT2 Population
papers.abstract: Background: The increasing use of genetic testing has identified thousands of KCNH2 variants associated with long QT syndrome type 2 (LQT2), yet most remain variants of uncertain significance (VUS). Translating functional abnormalities into clinically actionable evidence remains a major challenge. We established a nationwide functional genomics strategy to systematically characterize KCNH2 variants identified in the French LQT2 population and improve their clinical interpretation. Methods: We characterized 303 KCNH2 variants, including 201 VUS, using standardized high-throughput automated patch-clamp electrophysiology and complementary membrane trafficking assays. Nine electrophysiological parameters were integrated using MeTAL to predict variant-specific repolarization phenotypes under homozygous and heterozygous conditions. Modeled QTc values were compared with patient electrocardiographic data and variant-specific penetrance estimates. Functional evidence was calibrated against established benign and pathogenic variants using ClinGen-recommended categorical OddsPath and continuous likelihood-ratio approaches. Results: Multidimensional functional profiling revealed abnormalities not captured by current amplitude alone, identifying additional variants with clinically relevant repolarization defects. Among variants assessed under heterozygous conditions, MeTAL predictions showed 82.9% concordance with patient QTc phenotypes for ACMG class 5 variants, with apparent discordances partly consistent with incomplete penetrance. Continuous likelihood-ratio calibration demonstrated strong discrimination between established benign and pathogenic variants (AUC=0.936) and provided graded functional evidence for 76.1% of VUS. Integration of calibrated functional evidence into the ACMG/AMP framework enabled reclassification of 64 of 201 VUS (31.8%), including 7 as pathogenic, 46 as likely pathogenic, and 11 as likely benign. Conclusions: This nationwide study establishes a scalable framework integrating high-throughput electrophysiology, computational modeling, and clinical phenotyping to translate complex KCNH2 channel dysfunction into clinically interpretable evidence. The resulting reclassification of nearly one-third of VUS, together with the open-access HAMMER database, provides a resource to improve molecular diagnosis and risk assessment in LQT2.

papers.title: Expert-level localization of fine-grained cardiac structures across the transthoracic echocardiogram
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence models for echocardiography interpret studies without identifying the structures that support their outputs. We show that this spatial grounding does not emerge from the pretraining of current vision-language models. General-purpose and medical vision-language models and an open-vocabulary detector recalled 3% or fewer of cardiac structures and scored below a box that never sees the image. EchoLens, a detector trained on 5,912 expert-annotated structures and 4,219 Doppler signals from 136 patients, recalled 87% and localized structures as reliably as a blinded expert reader (box centre within the reference in 95.7% and 95.3% of cases). It covers 21 structures across 11 transthoracic views and 11 spectral Doppler signal types. In external data, two physicians judged 81-92% of its detections correct across all 11 views, and it identified the Doppler signal type in 83% of frames. EchoLens provides the spatial layer that grounded echocardiographic interpretation requires.

papers.title: Low-dose computed tomography and rapid molecular sputum testing in adults with suspected non-ventilator-associated hospital-acquired pneumonia: the HAP-FAST pilot sequential multiple assignment randomised trial with embedded qualitative and costing studies
papers.abstract: Background Non-ventilator-associated hospital-acquired pneumonia (nv-HAP) diagnosis is imprecise; chest x-rays (CXR) lack detail and sputum culture delays targeted prescribing. However, the evidence base to support diagnostic improvement is sparse. We assessed the feasibility of a trial of low-dose thoracic CT and rapid molecular testing of sputum. Methods HAP-FAST was a UK NIHR funded, open-label pilot sequential multiple assignment randomised trial with qualitative and costing substudies in four UK hospitals (ClinicalTrials.gov:NCT05483309). Using research without prior consent (RWPC) and site-stratified web-based randomisation, clinicians allocated adults with suspected nv-HAP (excluding pregnancy and palliation), before their second antibiotic dose, 1:1 to CT or CXR; participants subsequently treated for nv-HAP with sputum available underwent another 1:1 randomisation to BIOFIRE(R) FILMARRAY(R) Pneumonia plus Panel (FAPP) with standard microbiology or standard microbiology alone . Feasibility outcomes included recruitment, consent, intervention delivery and data completeness through 90 days. Adverse events were not systematically collected. Analyses were intention-to-treat and descriptive. Results Between June 2023 and March 2024, 220 adults were randomised at stage-1 (109 CT; 111 CXR), reaching target three months early. Of 154/220 (70.0%) subsequently managed as nv-HAP, 92/154 (59.7%) could not produce sputum. 62/154 (40.3%; 28.2% of stage-1) were randomised to stage-2: 31 FAPP and 31 no-FAPP. Allocated imaging was recorded for 75/109 (68.8%) CT and 99/111 (89.2%) CXR participants; 6/31(19.4%) FAPP tests were not completed. Consent for follow-up was obtained for 142/220 (64.5%). Protocol-defined clinical cure was assessable in 1/220 participants. The day-90 resource-use questionnaire was returned by 55/110 participants (50.0%). Qualitative findings supported RWPC but identified needs for staged communication, lower-burden follow-up and improved diagnostic pathways. Excess bed days and readmissions drove costs but data capture requires refinement. Conclusions A definitive trial is plausible only with enhanced RWPC, diagnostic delivery and follow-up pathways, improved sputum procedures, stewardship-aligned outcomes and routine economic data capture.

papers.title: LLM Representations Rival Traditional Predictors and Enhance Multimodal Prediction of APOE4 and Aβ-Burden
papers.abstract: Spontaneous language offers a scalable, noninvasive approach for identifying biological indicators of preclinical Alzheimer's disease (AD). We examined prediction of APOE4 carrier status and cerebral amyloid-beta burden using Cookie Theft picture descriptions from two cohorts of Hebrew- and English-speaking participants (IRAP, N=134; WRAP, N=1,541). Amyloid-beta burden was classified using lowest-quartile, median, and highest-quartile cutoffs, capturing accumulation below conventional amyloid-positivity thresholds. We compared embeddings from pretrained large language models (LLMs) with standard cognitive test scores, reflecting conventional clinical assessment, and theory-driven linguistic features, reflecting traditional language analysis. Embedding-based models achieved the highest F1 scores among constituent models in five of eight tasks involving APOE4 status and global amyloid-beta burden. High prediction disagreement suggested complementary signals across approaches. An any-positive ensemble significantly outperformed every constituent model and a prior-informed random baseline across all eight tasks, and significantly outperformed all constituent models in 21 of 24 regional amyloid-beta tasks. These findings highlight the complementarity of LLM-based, theory-driven, and cognitive measures for predicting AD-related genetic risk and amyloid pathology, and support further investigation of their potential for early screening approaches.

papers.title: MENTOR: An Evidence-Informed Large Language Model-Based Multi-Agent System for Efficient Selection of Institution-Specific Negative Control Outcomes
papers.abstract: Objective Negative control outcomes (NCOs) help detect and correct systematic error in observational studies, yet their selection remains largely manual. The Common Evidence Model (CEM) can generate candidate lists, but researchers must still screen them for plausibility as true nulls and for sufficient observation in each institution's data. We developed and evaluated MENTOR (Multi-agent Evidence-informed Negative conTrol Outcome selection with Reasoning), a multi-agent system of large language models (LLMs) that combines CEM evidence with LLM reasoning to select institution-specific NCOs. Methods Four LLM agents operate on an institution's Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership common data model. A Curator summarizes drug labels, a Suggester assesses locally frequent candidates with CEM evidence and a first-pass LLM judgment, an Adjudicator resolves their disagreements, and a Diagnostician relaxes the patient-count threshold until a target number of NCOs is met. Using Qwen3.6-27B, we evaluated 349 candidates for three drug pairs in a Korean tertiary hospital's electronic health records (2.9 million patients) against a blinded LLM judge from a different model family, validated by three experts on 90 candidates. We compared accuracy, positive predictive value (PPV), and sensitivity with CEM-only and first-pass-LLM-only selection. Results MENTOR proposed 243 NCOs versus 121 by CEM-only, with higher accuracy (0.83 [0.79-0.87] vs. 0.53 [0.48-0.58]), sensitivity (0.89 vs. 0.41), and PPV (0.86 vs. 0.79). Judge-expert agreement was {kappa}=0.63. Adjudication, needed for 44.1% of candidates, added little accuracy, and only with reasoning mode. Concordant acceptances, which bypass it, contained about half of the false positives. Only 7%-9% of CEM-proposed outcomes had at least 10,000 patients at the institution. Conclusion Combining LLM judgments with CEM evidence and local data yielded more NCOs, with higher PPV, than CEM alone. Restricting reasoning to discordant candidates kept computation time below 40% of that with reasoning in all agents. Every decision comes with its evidence and rationale for investigators' final review.

papers.title: Trait-Level Rather Than Individual-Level Resolution in Fitness Genomics: A Population-Calibrated Variant Prioritization Framework in a South Asian Cohort
papers.abstract: Translating candidate gene panels into objective physiological trait interpretations remains a major hurdle in exercise genomics. Conventional total genotype scoring suffers from severe panel-composition bias, fails to evaluate unannotated or novel variants, and frequently fosters inflated claims regarding individual athletic prediction. Here, we present a population-calibrated, multi-tiered computational framework that evaluates genomic variation across six evidence streams integrating deep learning protein and genomic language models (ESM-2, Evo 2), missense and splice predictors (AlphaMissense, SpliceAI), and regional pathogenic-density metrics to generate a continuous Variant Priority Score (VPS; 1-10 scale). By dynamically renormalizing missing evidence streams rather than zero-filling them, the framework robustly scores unannotated variants lacking empirical database entries. Individual trait burden across 344 genes (spanning 17 physiological traits in Aerobic, Anaerobic, and Recovery domains) is aggregated and normalized against ancestry-matched expectations derived from gnomAD South Asian and an in-house reference cohort (N > 13,000). When applied to 960 South Indian individuals (584 male, 376 female; whole-exome sequencing), this normalization removed the dependence of expected trait burden on panel size by construction, and gene count explained only 2.7% of the variance in the resulting capacity scores (six traits interrogated by 16 to 33 genes). Variance partitioning of 4,764 individual-by-trait scores (six of the 17 traits: one aerobic, two anaerobic and three recovery) revealed that score variation was predominantly trait-driven (45.5%) rather than individual-driven (11.1%, p = 0.386), a pattern reproduced independently in males and females and with no statistically significant gender difference in capacity scores, indicating that, in this cohort, the candidate panel resolved differences between physiological traits but did not detect differences between individuals in capacity scores (no athletic phenotype was measured). Benchmarking against ClinVar classifications achieved an AUC of 0.74, which fell to 0.62 when archive-dependent streams were excluded, directly quantifying the role of shared data provenance. Replacing the in-house frequency reference with gnomAD South Asian shifted absolute scores (median fold change 0.73) but preserved trait ordering (Spearman 0.96), so scores are positions against a stated, population-specific reference. This framework provides an auditable, evidence-traceable baseline for trait-level research and functional variant prioritization while offering a critical methodological safeguard against over-interpreting unvalidated individual performance predictions.

papers.title: Enrollees and Early Lessons from an Agentic Healthcare Platform with Physicians in the Loop
papers.abstract: Agentic healthcare platforms that combine large language models with physician oversight are growing quickly, but little is known about who uses them. We characterized 3,223 enrollees of Lotus AI, a free, physician-supervised agentic platform, who completed onboarding, messaged the agent, and had a linked health record between February and July 2026, and compared them with national benchmarks. Median age was 51 years and 62% were male. Chronic condition prevalence exceeded 2024 National Health Interview Survey estimates in every age band by 4 to 7 percentage points; 18% had a functional or symptom-defined disorder; among the 30% with four or more ambulatory visits in the prior year, care was spread across nearly five providers, with 44% meeting a threshold for high fragmentation. Users with functional disorders generated 1.8 times as many physician escalations and 2.6 times as many laboratory orders as other users, but no more prescriptions. This profile differs from the younger, predominantly female populations reported for direct-to-consumer telemedicine. It moves chronic disease management, functional disorder pathways, and care coordination from aspirations to design requirements, and we argue that deployed AI care platforms should characterize their populations against national benchmarks early.

papers.title: BenchmarkHub: an open-source platform for reproducible evaluation of large language models in healthcare
papers.abstract: Background: Large language models (LLMs) are solely judged by their scores on biomedical benchmarks, yet these scores are rarely reproducible since the prompts, inference settings and model builds are seldom reported. We developed BenchmarkHub, an open-source platform for auditable evaluation of language and vision-language models for biomedical research. Methods: BenchmarkHub is a Python web application (Django 5.2, SQLite) released under the MIT licence and available at https://github.com/juanjuanignacio/benchmarkhub. The application can be accessed through a browser interface, a set of command-line tools and a REST API, so interactive exploration and scripted pipelines produce identical, comparable records. The platform samples questions with fixed seeds, runs models directly or as tool-using agents in a code sandbox, grades answers with deterministic rules and stores every prompt, reply and tool call. The interface provides a leaderboard to rank performance of the models, allowing model comparison without any preexisting programming knowledge. Findings: We used BenchmarkHub to evaluate 12 open-weight models in five experiments on 15 biomedical benchmarks (11 text, two multimodal and two computational biology) and two general benchmarks. The pooled accuracy ranged from 46.1% (95% CI 43.0-49.3) to 80.9% (78.3-83.3). Re-grading the responses with simple answer-extraction rules lowered a model's accuracy by up to 33.1 percentage points, leading to a reorder of the leaderboard. Published scores were found for 23 out of the 143 benchmark/model combinations tested. The accuracy measured by BenchmarkHub was lower than in the published results in 19 out of the 23 available comparisons. The effect of four prompting protocols (1: default prompt; 2: asking the model to answer the letter only; 3: chain-of-thought prompting; 4: three-shot prompting) changed MedQA accuracy by up to 11.3 points but was not significant after multiple-testing correction with 150 questions. We also tested the impact of ablation on benchmarking using the MMMU benchmark dataset. Removing images lowered the accuracy by 18.0 and 19.3 points respectively for the two strongest models. Finally, the accuracy of agentic benchmarks using a sandboxed interpreter increased on computational biology tasks by 36-63 points. Interpretation: Benchmarking is essential to assess the impact and validity of LLMs for medical applications. BenchmarkHub allows a fair and rigorous comparison of models across established datasets, including the possibility to upload their own datasets. The suite includes visual tools to ease model comparison and ranking without any programming knowledge. Self-hosted infrastructure that records every choice and parameter makes benchmark claims checkable without data leaving the institution.

papers.title: Systematic Benchmarking and Optimization of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) for Clinical Phenotyping: A Type II Diabetes Case Study in an ICD-Screened Cohort
papers.abstract: Traditional EHR phenotyping methods can require substantial disease-specific development and long-term maintenance. While integrating large language models (LLMs) with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is promising, the impact of RAG configurations remains underexplored. We systematically evaluated these design choices for type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) phenotyping in an ICD-screened cohort. Using GPT-4o, we processed 170,678 clinical notes from 275 patients. We evaluated seven embedding models and three prompt strategies (baseline, improved zero-shot, and few-shot). Using the improved zero-shot prompt, we tested 350 embedding model-chunk size-retrieval depth combinations on the training set and selected eight optimized configurations for test-set evaluation. Combined with three prompts, these yielded 24 prompt-configuration combinations for comparison with ICD codes and the institutional PheNorm method. RAG achieved a mean sensitivity of 0.9019 (95% CI: 0.8866-0.9172), specificity of 0.7907 (0.7749-0.8066), PPV of 0.9405 (0.9365-0.9445), NPV of 0.6967 (0.6653-0.7281), and F1-score of 0.9204 (0.9124-0.9283). All combinations achieved higher PPV than ICD codes (0.7838). Compared with PheNorm, sensitivity was significantly higher (Holm-adjusted p < 0.001), while specificity differences were not significant. Paired bootstrap analyses showed higher NPV and F1-score , with no significant PPV difference. General-purpose embeddings showed higher sensitivity, whereas biomedical embeddings exhibited higher specificity and PPV. Few-shot prompting increased specificity and PPV but reduced sensitivity. Token usage varied substantially across embedding models. These findings suggest the importance of aligning RAG design with task-specific clinical priorities and token efficiency.
